title: Report: Trump mad RFK Jr. hasn’t cut more vaccines or proven autism link
gist: A Wall Street Journal report says Trump is frustrated that Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has not cut federal childhood vaccine recommendations further or produced a vaccine-autism link, despite Kennedy already stacking the vaccine advisory committee, dropping the hepatitis B birth dose and MMRV recommendations, and trimming the childhood schedule toward Denmark's. Courts have reversed some moves, December polling found the agenda broadly unpopular, and the piece flags succession chatter around Medicare chief Chris Klomp and CMS administrator Mehmet Oz.

insights.claim: Trump is reportedly pressuring Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to cut federal childhood vaccine recommendations further and to establish a vaccine-autism link, treating an autism remedy as a legacy project.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: US childhood vaccine demand is now driven by White House political preference rather than evidence, a persistent volume risk for pediatric vaccine franchises.
insights.locator: Trump has become fixated on the completely false

insights.claim: Trump reportedly told Kennedy in May that he had the yips preventing him from acting on his anti-vaccine agenda, and vented again in the Oval Office in June, indicating escalating repeated pressure rather than a one-off complaint.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Repeated presidential pressure means the policy direction is unlikely to stall on its own; expect further attempts at schedule cuts.

insights.so_what: A schedule cut is the largest addressable-dose reduction available to HHS without new legislation.

insights.claim: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. directed the CDC to stop promoting seasonal flu vaccines with prepaid advertisements during a particularly deadly flu season, and edited a CDC website to falsely link vaccines to autism.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole

insights.claim: Courts have already blocked two of Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s biggest vaccine moves, the advisory committee changes and the childhood vaccine schedule changes, showing litigation is a functioning offset to HHS action.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Judicial reversal risk means headline HHS announcements are not durable policy; fade the first-order reaction.

insights.claim: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is now laying regulatory groundwork to sabotage vaccination rates in ways that cannot be undone as easily in court, shifting from reversible announcements toward durable rulemaking.

insights.so_what: The next round of HHS vaccine actions is being designed to be litigation-proof, a structurally worse setup for vaccine makers.

insights.claim: December polling found that Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s efforts to cut vaccines were broadly unpopular and politically risky, which is why White House political advisors urged both Trump and Kennedy to tone down anti-vaccine rhetoric.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Public opinion is the main constraint on how far the agenda travels; midterm proximity should mechanically dampen visible action.
